newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Assembly passes bill to protect local taxes.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Assembly passes bill to protect local taxes.

text.p: California's Assembly approved legislation to protect an estimated 200 local taxes threatened by a controversial 1995 tax ruling, lawmakers said on Wednesday.
The lower house passed Assembly Bill 1362, by Assemblywoman Kerry Mazzoni, on a vote of 41-to-37, sending it to the Senate for review.
Under the bill, the state's requirement that local general taxes must be approved by the voters would not apply to taxes adopted prior to December 14, 1995, the effective date of the court ruling.

In 1986, California voters approved Proposition 62, an initiative that required local general taxes to be approved by local voters. Following its passage, several California courts ruled that the proposition was unconstitutional or not applicable to certain types of taxes.

But the state Supreme Court two years ago concluded that Proposition 62 was constitutional, effective December 14, 1995. That decision sent shock waves through California's local governments because it threatened an estimated 200 existing taxes.
The bill's supporters argued that in many cases, the tax funds had already been spent on police and fire services, funding libraries and paving roads.
Under Mazzoni's bill, the state Supreme Court's Proposition 62 decision would only apply to local taxes levied after the date of the court's decision.
